scope: Ordinary value-container ownership and timestamped scalar replay. Prior eight-scalar generic-state evidence is reused, not rerun. Source inspection precedes these expectations; observations do not generate them.

rules.VAL-17: A value retained beyond a cycle is an independent copy; later mutation of its source must not change the retained copy.
rules.borrow_boundary: Python assignment and native non-owning views are not declared owning copies. Their alias behavior is descriptive evidence, not automatically a VAL-17 failure.
rules.ordinary_timed_data: Three timed entries at MIN_ST plus 0, 3 and 6 microseconds with values 0, -7, -7 publish only at those times. Repeated equal scalar publication is a tick. Dense output [0,null,null,-7,null,null,-7] requires no slot capability in the source data.
rules.record: Retaining a copied timestamp/delta entry and replacing a store key must not mutate prior owned retained snapshots. Directly keeping an alias is tested and labelled separately.

descriptive_observations: Python ordinary list assignment, shallow copy, indexing, append and tuple-containing-list aliasing
Each Python authoring surface's GlobalState set/get aliasing and explicit deepcopy behavior; list annotation support may fail and is not repaired by claiming tuple parity
Native mutable-list view/index/set/push, immutable-list mutation refusal, explicit Value copy/clone, tuple-contained list copy and GlobalState borrowed mutation
Native direct-const source uses public native node authoring with ordinary scalar list data; this is not a claim of an existing built-in const-data replay overload
The existing Python replay operator takes a key; ordinary timed iterable seeding is a separate route from authoring a const-data generator
Any unsupported type, construction, or API outcome remains an error/missing measurement, never substituted with expected data
